newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most Germans doubt joblessness to be halved -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Germans doubt joblessness to be halved -- poll.

text.p: Ninety-one percent of Germans do not think record unemployment can be cut in half by the year 2000 as the government has promised, according to a recent poll.
Seventy-three percent of those asked also said they do not agree with Bonn's funding cuts for jobs programmes, the poll this week for public television station ARD showed.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl last year set a goal of halving joblessness by 2000 through an "Alliance for Jobs" of labour, employers and politicians.
But with the number of unemployed at 4.1 million, Bonn's budget cuts to meet EU economic and monetary union requirements have come under increasing criticism.
The poll showed 51 percent did not think an "Alliance for Jobs" could greatly improve the situation, against 40 percent who did.
